conventions.convention: Clifford vectors satisfy v²=Q(v)1; real signatures (p,q) count positive squares first and negative squares second.
Graded tensor multiplication is (a⊗b)(a′⊗b′)=(-1)^(|b||a′|)aa′⊗bb′; graded-module isomorphisms preserve parity.
The matrix classification assumes finite-dimensional nondegenerate real or complex forms; the parity and orthogonal-sum results also allow degenerate forms.
Coefficient type D refers to the endomorphism algebra Dᵒᵖ of the simple even-algebra column module, with split factors counted separately.
In dimension zero the Clifford algebra is purely even; its two graded-simple modules are the one-dimensional modules placed in the two different parities.

load_bearing.statement: As ungraded real algebras, Cl(p+1,q+1)≅Cl(p,q)⊗M₂(R), Cl(n+2,0)≅Cl(0,n)⊗M₂(R), and Cl(0,n+2)≅Cl(n,0)⊗H for p,q,n≥0. Both pure-signature families have eightfold matrix periodicity with factor M₁₆(R).

For nondegenerate real forms, the displayed matrix-algebra table is indexed by n=p+q and p−q modulo eight. For nondegenerate complex forms, Cl_n(C)≅M_(2^(n/2))(C) for even n, and two copies of M_(2^((n−1)/2))(C) for odd n.
If p>0, Cl(p,q)⁰≅Cl(q,p−1); if p=0 and q>0, Cl(0,q)⁰≅Cl(0,q−1). For standard complex dimension n>0, Cl_n(C)⁰≅Cl_(0,n−1)(C)≅Cl_(n−1)(C).

Let A=A⁰⊕A¹ be a graded unital associative algebra over a field containing an invertible odd element. Taking M⁰ gives a bijection between graded-simple A-module classes with even isomorphisms and simple A⁰-module classes; induction A⊗_(A⁰)N is its inverse.
C⊗_R C≅C⊕C, C⊗_R H≅M₂(C), H⊗_R H≅M₄(R), and M_m(D)⊗_R M_n(E)≅M_(mn)(D⊗_R E) for D,E∈{R,C,H} and positive m,n.

For finite-dimensional quadratic spaces over a field of characteristic not two, the canonical map Cl(V⊕W,Q⊕R)→Cl(V,Q)⊗̂Cl(W,R), sending (v,w) to v̄⊗1+1⊗w̄, is a graded algebra isomorphism, without a nondegeneracy assumption.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.1 says, in the q>p branch, “with s=q-p” and then substitutes n=8t+s+2m. Step 1.2 defined s as the residue of the remaining pure dimension, so the intended relation is q-p=8t+s, 0≤s<8. The wording is inconsistent when q-p≥8; for example (p,q)=(0,9) has t=1,s=1, not s=9. The table itself agrees with the recurrence calculation.

alerts.finding: In thm-complex-spin-modules-and-compact-reducibility, step 1.1 chooses a “pairwise orthogonal anisotropic real basis e_1,...,e_n” and separately defines normalized vectors u_i=e_i/√|Q(e_i)|. Step 2.1 nevertheless says “Set ω=i^m e_1⋯e_(2m); the Clifford relations show ω²=1”. For the chosen, potentially unnormalized e_i, the square is ∏Q(e_i), not necessarily 1. In positive dimension two, e_1=2f_1 and e_2=f_2 for an orthonormal basis gives ω²=4, so the asserted p_±=(1±ω)/2 are not idempotents. The proof needs an explicit normalization at this use.

seams_checked.note: The quotient, plus-square relation, universal property, polarized anticommutation, and PBW dimension are used with their actual characteristic and finite-dimensional hypotheses. Degenerate forms remain allowed precisely in the grading and orthogonal-sum results.

The page and inspected citation interfaces consistently translate C_n to Cl(0,n). The even-part equivalence excludes n=0, restriction matrices match the negative-square table, and graded tensor periodicity is supported by a separate local graded Morita argument.

The real spinor theorem uses the even-algebra signatures and matrix factors, distinguishing Clifford spinor restrictions from arbitrary Spin representations. Complex half-spin sizes faithfully use the complex classification and even-subalgebra identification. The separate volume-normalization proof defect is recorded in alerts.
